interface.title: Phylogenetic Tree Generator (DNA Clustering with K-mers)
interface.stage_of_work: Exploratory analysis: quick alignment-free comparison of whole sequences (here mitochondrial genomes of about 16.5 kb) before or instead of an alignment-based phylogeny
interface.what_it_is_for: Upload several species' FASTA sequences, turn each into a k-mer profile, compute pairwise Manhattan, Jaccard or Cosine distances, and see and export a UPGMA dendrogram of the species.

data.note: I uploaded the six test files: HomoSapiens, Chimpanzee, gorilla, orangutan, rhesusmacaque and zebrafish .fasta, each about 16.4–16.6 kb. I first uploaded HomoSapiens alone to test the one-file case, then added the other five. Later I removed zebrafish for a 5-species run.

tree.general: Infer and compare relationships among a set of sequences without aligning them, and take the results elsewhere
tree.specific: Build k-mer distance matrices and UPGMA dendrograms for primate and zebrafish mitochondrial FASTA files, compare metrics and k values, and download CSV and PNG

features.name: Parameter-guarded run panel for an alignment-free distance tree
features.general: Load a set of files, set a numeric resolution parameter that warns at low values, choose one of several similarity measures, then press one Run button that checks some inputs first
features.specific: Sidebar with a multi-file FASTA uploader, a k-mer size field (2–15, warning below 5), a distance method dropdown (manhattan, jaccard, cosine) and Compute Matrix & Generate Tree. Compute warns when no method is chosen or when no files are loaded. Despite the message text ('at least two FASTA files'), a single file is not caught and crashes with a ValueError. Per the reviewer's reading of the code (app.py:345–357), both warnings are skipped once a run has stored a dendrogram
steps: Upload two or more FASTA files (more can be added later; remove one with ×)
Set k by typing or with −/+ (out-of-range values are rejected; k<5 shows a warning)
Pick a distance method from the dropdown
Press Compute Matrix & Generate Tree; a message confirms 'Processing N sequences with k = … and method = …'
serves_tasks: Load the sequences to compare, one file per taxon
Choose the word length for sequence profiles
Choose how dissimilarity between profiles is measured
Get told when the inputs are not ready
Re-run the analysis on a subset of the items

features.name: Summary → distance matrix → dendrogram results stack
features.general: After one run, show a per-item summary table, the pairwise distance matrix, and a hierarchical-clustering tree titled with the parameters used, so that reruns with other settings can be compared
features.specific: Sequence Summary (species, sequence length, unique k-mers), Distance Matrix table, and a UPGMA Dendrogram titled 'UPGMA Dendrogram (k=…, method=…)'; changing method or k and recomputing redraws all three
steps: Read the per-species length and unique k-mer counts
Read the pairwise distances in the matrix
Read the dendrogram, whose title names k and method
Change method or k, recompute, and compare tree shape and distance scale
serves_tasks: Build pairwise distances and a hierarchical-clustering tree for all items
Check each input's length and profile size before trusting the distances
Compare how the choice of distance measure changes distances and tree shape
See how the word-length parameter affects resolution and tree topology
Judge each tree against known relationships to decide which settings to trust

features.name: Export of the last run's table and figure
features.general: Export the latest results as a CSV with a parameter header, the per-item summary and the full-precision matrix, and the figure as a PNG. The buttons stay after the page refreshes. The parameter header reflects the settings at download time, not necessarily those of the run
features.specific: Download Distance Matrix with Summary (CSV) writes '# Distance Method', '# k-mer Size', '# Sequence Summary' and '# Distance Matrix' blocks; Download Dendrogram (PNG) writes dendrogram.png. The summary, matrix and figure come from the most recent Compute. Per the reviewer's reading of the code (app.py:314–315), the two header lines are read from the live sidebar widgets, so changing k or the method after Compute mislabels the CSV
steps: Without changing k or method, click Download Distance Matrix with Summary (CSV)
After a new run, download again to get the updated files
serves_tasks: Save the distance table with its parameters and per-item summary
Save the tree figure as an image

features.specific: 'Read This First: Tips for Getting Meaningful Results' expander, open by default, covering small vs. large k and what Jaccard, Manhattan and Cosine each measure; clicking its header collapses it
steps: Open the app; the tips panel is already expanded

screens_never_reached: A valid tree from a single uploaded file: with one file the 'at least two files' check is not applied, and the app crashes with 'ValueError: The number of observations cannot be determined on an empty distance matrix' (screens/011.webp)
not_done: Pressing Compute with only one file loaded is a dead end: the Sequence Summary appears, then a ValueError traceback (empty distance matrix) (screens/011.webp). Removed from the tree as a crash.
I could not open the downloaded dendrogram.png. The download reports only its size (26,260 bytes, binary), so I could not check its image content against the on-screen tree.
The Sequence Summary grid's own 'Download as CSV' icon produced no captured download (screens/038.webp). This is probably the browser save API Streamlit uses, which this browser does not catch.
I did not open the Distance Matrix table's toolbar. It is drawn as a static table with numbered header rows and columns (0–6), not as an interactive grid.

Clicking any download button reruns the app: the summary, matrix and dendrogram disappear from the page and only the two download buttons remain (screens/017.webp). Those buttons also stay after k or method changes, until the next Compute (screens/028.webp), so they offer the previous run's results. The CSV's '# Distance Method' and '# k-mer Size' header is taken from the current sidebar values, not the stored run (per the reviewer's reading of app.py:314–315), so in that state it would mislabel the data. I did not test this.
In the replay, the dendrogram's fullscreen view at 1280 px wide cut off the right side of the figure (joins near the root, beyond about 0.65) (check/screens/026.webp, check/screens/027.webp).
I did not try the sidebar collapse button and the Streamlit menu (⋮/Deploy). They are general Streamlit page controls, not part of this tool, and the collapse click timed out once.
I did not try every combination of method and k. I sampled manhattan k=5, jaccard k=5, cosine k=5, jaccard k=8, manhattan k=2 and manhattan k=7 on 5 species.
